prompt: Give RouteHistory a copy constructor -- Java's normal substitute for clone() -- so copying a route shares nothing with the original. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Object.clone and the Cloneable interface are awkward enough that a copy constructor, a constructor taking another instance of the same class, is the idiomatic way to duplicate an object. Copying the list reference would only give the two routes the same ArrayList, so both would change together; new ArrayList<>(other.stops) or addAll makes an independent list. The same reasoning applies to the ordinary constructor, which must not keep the caller's list either.
hints: Both constructors should copy the stops rather than store the list they were handed -- addAll or new ArrayList<>(...) are both fine.
The copy constructor can reach other.stops directly: private is per class, not per object.
String.join(" -> ", stops) builds the route text, and List.equals already compares two lists element by element in order.
